newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein meets Israeli opposition leader.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein meets Israeli opposition leader.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein and newly elected Israeli opposition leader Ehud Barak on Monday discussed obstacles facing the Middle East peace process and efforts to get it back on track, the state news agency said.

A Jordanian official, quoted by state news agency Petra, said the king discussed with Barak, who arrived on a short visit to Amman, "ways of overcoming the hurdles which face the Middle East peace process" and the "need to pull together every effort to resume negotiations".

The official said their discussions emphasised the "need to get views closer to get out of the deadlock which the peace process is facing, to prepare the way for a resumption of talks between the Palestinians and Israelis."

King Hussein also presented Barak, at a reception in the Royal Raghdan Palace attended by Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali, with a symbolic present to commemorate his landslide victory in the race for leader of Israel's main opposition Labour party.

The Labour-led government ousted last year by the right wing Likud party headed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu struck an interim peace deal with the Palestinians and signed a peace treaty with Jordan during its tenure.
It was guided by the principle of trading occupied Arab land for peace. Netanyahu opposes trading land for peace but has said he will uphold deals signed by the previous government.
